questions.question: When you prepare to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing. This helps you see ahead better and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you carry a heavy load, you should adjust the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, springs, air shocks, and dampers to the settings for that weight.

questions.question: Eye protection, such as goggles or a face shield, is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required for all riders. You can use goggles, a face shield, glasses, or an approved windshield.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, pick a lane position where other drivers can see you best. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. Slow down as you approach. Do not speed up or change position suddenly, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: Which factor does not affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also matter.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is in the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose the position that gives you the best visibility and most space around you. Move your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been previously worn in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been previously worn in an accident.
questions.explanation: For best protection, choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly all around, and has no visible damage. Replace a helmet if it was worn during a crash.

questions.question: An engine will seize due to:
questions.correctAnswerText: A lack of oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when oil runs low. Without oil, the engine's moving parts cannot slide smoothly against each other, and the engine overheats.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to be split up.
The riders will get to their destination more quickly in a close group than a group that is spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The riders will get to their destination more quickly in a close group than a group that is spread out.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than riding spread out because it uses less road space, is easier for others to see, and helps prevent the group from getting separated at traffic lights and during passing.

questions.question: To see better when you are about to pass a vehicle on its left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass or bridge ahead is low. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle means yield. Slow down to a safe speed and stop if needed. Stop at a marked stop line if one exists.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, what will your steering feel like?
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop right away and check your tires.

questions.question: In hot weather, should you wear a riding jacket?

options.text: Yes, it helps protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat-related problems.
Only if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, plus other injuries.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake. Never brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do about space?

options.text: Increase your normal space around each rider.
Keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: Ride close together as a group, but always keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: On a wet road, which part of a lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of a lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. When wet, this strip is slippery. Ride to the side of this strip, even though you are still in the middle area of the lane.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, where is the safest place to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
On the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center strip. Ride in the tire tracks made by other vehicles. The left track is often safest.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run along the road, at what angle should you cross?
questions.correctAnswerText: At a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross at least at a 45-degree angle. Make a quick, sharp turn to cross. If you go slowly or at a shallow angle, the tracks can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tighten the chain
questions.explanation: Tightening the chain may fix chain slippage. If tightening does not solve the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: The middle of the lane often has an oily strip. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining
Ride only on the oily strip because it gives better grip
Avoid the entire center of the lane
Not worry about oil or debris in the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually still has enough grip for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it while still staying in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see
Ride only on the left side of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another vehicle), use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see, and wear reflective materials to be seen. Always change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen better, and stay safe.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle has a sidecar, the passenger should ride in the sidecar. The passenger must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Removes your ability to change direction
Is only a problem if the front tire also skids

questions.correctAnswerText: Removes your ability to change direction
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a violent crash with serious injury or death. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the wheel locks, you cannot steer. To regain control, release the brake.

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil from cars often collect
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars often collect
questions.explanation: Debris and oil from cars collect in the center of lanes. Hazards like utility hole covers can also be found in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection
Yield only to traffic on the right
Yield only to traffic on the left
Slow down and let other traffic go first

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let traffic in the intersection or on the road you are entering go first.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake
Brake and swerve at the same time
Choose to either brake or swerve
Do not swerve and only use the front brake to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders rarely hear a tire going flat. You will usually notice a tire problem by how the motorcycle handles instead.
